senses.gloss:
cidākāśa
(‘space or ether of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्’)
------------------------------------------
The उपनिषद्स् describe आकाश (generally translated as space or ether) as the body of ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute. This आकाश is also, sometimes, identified with bliss. However, the आकाश, in these statements should not be confused with the ‘bhūtākāśa,’ or elemental आकाश, but must be understood as ‘cidākāśa,’ or plane of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्. Some Śaiva philosophers like श्रीकण्ठ (13th cent. A. D.) consider it as the ultimate material principle (‘parāprakṛti’), the same as ultimate energy. It is the energy of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्, otherwise called चिच्छक्ति also. It is the original force of life that manifests itself in the activities of life. All kinds of life functions and all experiences of pleasure are based on the lower or higher level of this चिदाकाश.
See also CICCHAKTI.

Cidambaram
(‘ether of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्’)
------------------------------------------
Pilgrimage to holy places has become a part of a Hindu’s life. Such places are generally associated with अवतार-puruṣas (incarnations of God), ṛṣis (sages) or other holy persons. And, they are mostly situated in places of great natural beauty conducive to spiritual pursuits.
One of the most famous places of पिल्ग्रिमगे in South India which draws thousands of votaries even from Sri Lanka, is चिदम्बरम् (Chidambaram), called ‘Tillai’ in Tamil. It is about 230 kms. (150 miles) to the south-west of Madras city and is situated in the south Arcot district of Tamil Nadu. It is one of the ‘pañca-liṅgas’ (emblems of शिव representing the five elements) and houses the ‘ākāśaliṅga’ (‘emblem of the ether principle’). The original icon of the famous नटराज (See NAṬARĀJA.), made of gold, is kept in the ‘Kanaka सभा’ (‘golden hall’), one of the five spacious halls in the temple complex. The hall itself gets its name due to the fact of its roof being covered with golden plates. (kanaka = gold).
Most of the places of Hindu पिल्ग्रिमगे have a ‘sthalapurāṇa,’ a local legend, explaining the significance of the place and its holy associations. As per the local legend of चिदम्बरम्, this is the place where शिव defeated Bhadrakālī in a dance contest and blessed his devotees, the sages पतञ्जलि (incarnation of the serpent deity आदिशेष) and Vyāghrapada. Local tradition holds the temple to be about 2000 years old.
Sprawling over an area of 13 hectares (32 acres), the नटराज temple complex stands on an alluvial plain between two rivers. Built entirely of dressed granite—though no granite has been found within a radius of about 77 kms. (50 miles)—it is surrounded by nine meter (30 ft.) high boundary walls. There are several gopurams or gateways, one facing the east rising in nine tiers, being the most beautiful. It is exquisitely decorated with friezes depicting scenes from Hindu mytho-logy. Two of the gopurams attached to the inner wall of the main temple exhibit 108 poses of dance taught in the नाट्यशास्त्र or the science of dance. There are several subsidiary temples in the complex, dedicated to Śivakāmī (Pārvatī, the consort of शिव), Govindarāja (Viṣṇu), Puṇḍarīkavallī (Lakṣmī) and गणेश. The icon of गणेश here is said to be the largest in size, in the whole of India. There is also the main temple tank called ‘Śivagaṅgā’ measuring 45 m. by 30 m. (150’ by 100’) with steps all round. The thousand pillared hall near this tank is associated with Sekkizhar (11th cent. A. D.) who is said to have composed his monumental work Peria-purāṇam (‘the Great म्य्थोलोग्य्’ containing the biographies of Śaivite saints of Tamil Nadu) here.
To the right of the icon of नटराज, on the background wall, there is a यन्त्र (geometrical symbol of the deity) adorned with golden necklaces. This is the place of the ‘ākāśaliṅga’ and is known as ‘cidambara-rahasya,’ the ‘secret’ of चिदम्बरम्. It is kept covered by a screen which is pushed aside twice a day for facilitating the devotees to view it.
Though built in stages by several kings like Kulottuṅga II (A. D. 1135-1150), Sundara Pāṇḍya II (c. 1250), and कृष्ण-devarāya (A.D. 1509-1529), the architectural harmony has been maintained and it is of the Coḷa style. In fact, the deity was the family God of the Coḷa dynasty.
The biggest festival at the चिदम्बरम् temple is ‘Tiruvādirai’ which falls during December-January. Since it is a शिव temple, Mahāśivarātri is of course, celebrated in a grand manner.
